summary: B03 is delivered: synthetic pointer, scroll, and key commands route through GPUI's native pipeline, input.rs is diagnostic-free, and all six input tests pass. B04 delivered the native focus primitive (dispatch_focus calls Window::focus(&FocusHandle) with no key event) but its named-node half is blocked because gpui-pre 0.3.6 exposes no node-id to FocusHandle path from outside the crate; TypeText/ReplaceText now return Unsupported pending C04.

B03-SYNTHETIC-INPUT-ROUTING.evidence: Pointer commands build the same MouseMove/MouseDown/MouseUp/ScrollWheel PlatformInput variants as before and dispatch them with Window::dispatch_event (input.rs:109); keystrokes use Window::dispatch_keystroke, which builds PlatformInput::KeyDown and calls Window::dispatch_event internally (gpui-pre window.rs:5373-5382) and then feeds key_char to the active input handler, so key bindings and text entry keep the native path. Evidence: cargo check -p gpui-mcp --tests reports zero diagnostics in input.rs, and in the scratch run synthetic_mouse_move_runs_gpui_hover_handlers (move), synthetic_platform_drag_runs_gpui_drag_and_drop_handlers (click/down/move/up), synthetic_scroll_wheel_runs_gpui_scroll_handlers, and synthetic_keystroke_runs_focused_element_key_handlers all pass.

B04-FOCUS-NAVIGATION.evidence: Handle-based half verified: dispatch_focus(handle, window, cx) calls Window::focus(&FocusHandle) (gpui-pre window.rs:2302) and dispatch_focus_moves_focus_without_a_key_event passes with no key event dispatched. Named-node half unreachable from outside the crate: A11y is pub(crate) (window/a11y.rs:126), focus_ids is pub(crate) (window/a11y.rs:149), FocusHandle::for_id is pub(crate) (window.rs:558), App::focus_handles is pub(crate) (window.rs:760), and the only native accesskit::NodeId-to-focus path is handle_a11y_action, also pub(crate) (window.rs:6805; Action::Focus branch 6847-6853); no public Window/App method maps a node id or accesskit::NodeId to a FocusHandle. service.rs:601 (B05) therefore still cannot resolve a node id. Needs a Batch C visibility item (for example a public Window::focus_a11y_node(accesskit::NodeId, cx) -> bool wrapping the existing branch, with the observer retaining each node's accesskit_id from debug_a11y_tree_json) plus bridge-side resolution in observer.rs/service.rs, or an owner-approved bridge API for applications to register FocusHandles.

risks: Text entry is temporarily narrowed: InputCommand::TypeText and ReplaceText return ErrorCode::Unsupported (message cites C04) because Window::input_handlers is pub(crate) (window.rs:989); the MCP type_text/set_text tools report that error until Batch C lands.
The Batch B gate cargo check --workspace cannot exit 0 from this branch: service.rs:601 and lib.rs:71 are B05-owned; input.rs itself is clean under the scoped check.

In that run two observer.rs tests fail because debug_a11y_tree_json() returns None on a fresh window until C02 activates the a11y tree; this is external to this task's file but material to B02/B06 integration.

Alternative route if the owner prefers no focus-map patch: once C03 exposes node bounds, the already-rewired pointer path can move focus to a named node by clicking its center (the protocol documents NodeAction::Focus as a center click), but that route does not go through Window::focus(&FocusHandle) as the acceptance names.

It needs a Batch C visibility item or an owner scope decision, and the bridge-side resolution spans observer.rs and service.rs, outside this task's ownership.
